speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing intense itching and red bumps on your thigh and other parts of your body; can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they are itchy at night?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies. The combination of intense nocturnal itching, new-onset papular rash on the thigh, and the patient's recent travel to a high-density environment (business conference) is highly suggestive of scabies infestation caused by *Sarcoptes scabiei* mites. REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin exam showing burrows and vesicles.
